issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter missing @MainActor annotation
issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31198 - EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings

structured_output.summary:
This PR is a string-only base for splitting the Studies toggle in Firefox iOS and adding a new Rollouts toggle. It adds v148 keys for Studies and Rollouts to `Strings.swift` and to the en-GB and en-CA `Settings.strings` files, adds an exclusion to the reference-string linter config, and adds new `*V2`/Rollouts constants plus a `SettingsTextFormatter` helper to the Focus `UIConstants.swift`. Nothing in the PR consumes the new constants yet, so runtime behaviour is unchanged.

The Firefox iOS additions follow the existing V2 pattern closely: keys, tableName, values and translator comments match between `Strings.swift` and the `.strings` files, except for one comment. The `RolloutsSettingMessage` translator comment says `%1$@` while its value and the `.strings` comment use `%@`. The repo's l10n README says comments must reference every placeable, so the reference-string linter will likely fail on this PR. The Focus side has a real defect: `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText` reads the old `detailTextStudies` key instead of the new `detailTextStudiesV2`, so any caller wiring the new Studies toggle would show the old copy. The helper is unused today, so this is latent, but it should be fixed before anyone calls it. The remaining items are minor: an unneeded quotes exclusion, unrelated curly-to-straight quote churn in Focus comments, and out-of-order keys in the `.strings` files.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `%1$@` versus `%@` mismatch in the Rollouts message comment is a correctness issue in the reference strings: it will likely fail this repo's l10n linter on the PR and gives translators a wrong placeholder hint. The Focus formatter reading the wrong key is a latent bug that should be fixed before the follow-up PR wires it up. The other findings are low-severity cleanup.

architecture.overview:
Firefox iOS localizes Settings text through `Strings.swift`, which wraps `MZLocalizedString` keys in the `Settings` table, and the matching `Settings.strings` files in `firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files`. The en-US reference strings are checked in CI by `moz-xliff-lint` using `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`, which enforces brand names, typography, and placeable comments. Focus has a separate table, `UIConstants.strings` in `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, which uses `NSLocalizedString` with inline English fallbacks.

This PR adds v148 entries for the Studies and Rollouts settings to both systems. Firefox iOS gets three new Studies constants (V3) and three new Rollouts constants, plus matching entries in en-GB and en-CA `Settings.strings` and one linter exclusion. Focus gets new `.v2` Studies and Send Usage keys, a Rollouts pair, and a `SettingsTextFormatter` helper class. No UI code reads any of these constants yet, so the PR only changes what strings exist, not what the app displays.
steps: Start at the boundary: `Strings.swift` declares `Strings.*` constants that call `MZLocalizedString(key:tableName:value:comment:)`, and the matching key/value pairs live in `Settings.strings` for en-GB and en-CA.

The PR appends Studies V3 constants (`StudiesSettingTitleV3`, `StudiesSettingLinkV3`, `StudiesSettingMessageV3`) and Rollouts constants (`RolloutsSettingTitle`, `RolloutsSettingLink`, `RolloutsSettingMessage`) to `Strings.swift`, using `v148` keys.

The same keys are added to the en-GB and en-CA `Settings.strings` files, with values and translator comments mirroring the Swift constants. The Rollouts comment is where the placeholder mismatch appears.
`linter_config_ios.json` gains a quotes exclusion for `Settings.Studies.Message.v148`, which the reference-string linter reads during CI.

On the Focus side, `UIConstants.strings` gains `*V2` Studies/Send Usage keys and Rollouts keys, and a new nested `SettingsTextFormatter` singleton wraps two `String(format:)` calls. The Studies formatter reads the old key, and nothing calls the formatter yet.
Nothing in the PR yet connects these constants or formatter to a settings screen, so the follow-up toggle split is where the runtime effect will appear.

findings.title: Rollouts message comment placeholder does not match its value
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, the `RolloutsSettingMessage` constant (around lines 6257-6261) has a translator comment that says `%1$@ is the app name`, but its value uses a plain `%@` placeholder. Change the comment so it references `%@` instead of `%1$@`, matching the comment in the `Settings.Rollouts.Message.v148` entry of the en-GB and en-CA `Settings.strings` files. The l10n README (`.github/l10n/README.md`) requires comments to reference each placeable in the text, which is what the reference-string linter enforces. Change only the comment text.

findings.title: Focus SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText uses the old Studies copy
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText(appName:)` (around line 424) passes `strings.detailTextStudies` to `String(format:)`. That key still holds the old copy. Change it to `strings.detailTextStudiesV2`, which this PR adds (around line 207) for the new Studies toggle text. Match the way `formatRolloutsText` (around line 428) uses its new key. Do not change any other behaviour.

findings.title: New SettingsTextFormatter singleton is unused and adds no value
findings.body:
`SettingsTextFormatter` is a singleton (`static let shared`, `private init()`) with two one-line `String(format:)` wrappers. Nothing in the repo calls it or any of the new Focus `*V2`/Rollouts constants (grep finds only the definitions). Because the PR is meant as a base for a later change, the constants can stay, but a formatter that nothing uses is dead code. It also already had the bug in the previous finding. The class would be simpler as a call site inside the settings screen, added in the PR that needs it.

::code{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="418-430"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, the `SettingsTextFormatter` class (around lines 418-430) is never referenced anywhere in the repo. Either delete it, or keep the `strings` constants and move the formatting into the Focus settings screen that will consume them, in the same PR that wires up the toggle. Confirm with grep that no call sites exist before removing it. Leave the `*V2`/Rollouts `NSLocalizedString` constants in place for the follow-up work.

findings.title: Quotes exclusion added for a string that has no quote characters
findings.body:
The new quotes exclusion `firefox-ios.xliff:Settings.Studies.Message.v148` covers a value that contains no straight or curly quotes: `"%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone."`. An exclusion that isn't needed silences the typography check for that key, so a future quote typo in the source would pass unnoticed. I couldn't run `moz-xliff-lint` here to confirm the check fires, so this depends on whether the exclusion was copied from another key. If the linter passes without it, remove it.

::diff{file=".github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json" lines="6-10"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`, the `quotes` block (around lines 6-10) adds an exclusion for `firefox-ios.xliff:Settings.Studies.Message.v148`. That source string contains no quote characters, so the exclusion probably isn't needed. Remove it, leaving `"exclusions": []`, and confirm the reference-string linter still passes. If the linter does flag this key, document why in the PR and keep the exclusion.

findings.title: Unrelated quote-style churn in existing Focus comments
findings.body:
The PR changes the existing comments on `detailTextSendUsageData` and `detailTextStudies` from curly quotes (`“Firefox Focus” or ”Firefox Klar”`) to escaped straight quotes (`\"Firefox Focus\"`). These are not part of the new feature. The l10n README lists `""` instead of `“”` as a typography error, so the straight quotes move the comments away from the house style. The Focus linter may read these comments, so I'm not certain this lint-clean, but the change is still unrelated to the PR and should be reverted to keep the diff focused.

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="202-205"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, revert the comment changes on `detailTextSendUsageData` (around line 202) and `detailTextStudies` (around line 205). Restore the original curly quotes `“Firefox Focus”` and `”Firefox Klar”` instead of the escaped straight quotes. Keep the new `*V2`/Rollouts constants as they are. Confirm the diff is limited to the new constants and the formatter.

findings.title: Rollouts keys inserted out of alphabetical order in the Settings.strings files
findings.body:
The `Settings.Rollouts.*.v148` entries go between `Settings.Studies.*` and `Settings.Summarize.*`. The rest of the file is sorted by key, so `Settings.Rollouts` belongs before `Settings.Search`. Out-of-order keys make later sorted-merge or re-sort tools produce noisy diffs and make the key easy to miss when scanning. The same placement appears in both en-GB and en-CA.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files/en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings" lines="253-260"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files/en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings` and `en-CA.lproj/Settings.strings`, move the three `Settings.Rollouts.*.v148` entries (Link, Message, Title, with their comments) so they sit alphabetically among the other `Settings.*` keys, before `Settings.Search...`. Keep the keys, values and comments unchanged, and keep each file's existing sort order.

findings.title: v148 Firefox iOS strings follow the existing V2 pattern and match across files
findings.body: The new Firefox iOS constants in `Strings.swift` use the same shape as the existing `StudiesSettingTitleV2`/`...V2` constants. Keys are versioned (`.v148`), tableName is `Settings`, and each Studies key/value/comment matches its `Settings.strings` entry in both en-GB and en-CA. The Studies message's `%@` placeholder and its comment agree. Only the Rollouts message comment diverges, which is covered by the high-severity finding.
